findings: SCOPE: 15 WebSearch calls plus 5 WebFetch/pdftotext reads. Verified from full text: Trust or Escalate (2407.18370) and Semantic Agreement cascades (2509.21837) and Ding's agreement audit (2607.08065). Everything else is from search-result abstracts/snippets (labeled 'snippet-level'); formulas marked (std) are standard textbook definitions I am supplying, not quoted from a fetched page.

CASCADE RECIPE (FrugalGPT, 2305.05176, snippet-level): cascade of length 3; a DistilBERT regression scorer takes (query, answer, model) and outputs a reliability score; a per-step threshold and the model ordering are learned jointly as a budget-constrained optimization on a TRAIN split, evaluated on a random held-out TEST split. Headline: matches GPT-4 at up to 98% lower cost, or +4% accuracy at equal cost. Note this learned scorer is exactly the 'learned allocator' that your RL claim 1 says a label-free confidence threshold is not beaten by; for AR3 the FrugalGPT-style learned scorer is the strongest 'learned' baseline a reviewer will name.

TRUST OR ESCALATE (Jung, Brahman, Choi, ICLR 2025, arXiv 2407.18370, verified from full text). Setup: judge f_LM with confidence c_LM; accept verdict iff c_LM >= lambda else abstain/escalate. Risk R(lambda) = P(f != human AND c >= lambda) conditioned on acceptance; empirical R_hat(lambda) = mean over the n(lambda) accepted calibration items of 1{f != y_human}. Threshold chosen by multiple testing: exact Clopper-Pearson-style binomial upper confidence bound R+(lambda) at level 1-delta; fixed-sequence testing (Bauer 1991) scans lambda from highest (0.999) downward and stops at the last lambda whose bound is <= alpha; Theorem 1: with prob >= 1-delta over the calibration draw, the selective risk is <= alpha. Config: |Dcal|=500, delta=0.1, 1000 random cal/test splits; they report 'guarantee success rate' (fraction of splits where test risk <= alpha, should be ~>=90%) plus coverage. Cascade: each judge in order gets its own lambda_i, only uncertain items escalate; GPT-4 used last; headline: cascade starting with Mistral-7B guarantees >80% human agreement at ~80% coverage where GPT-4 alone rarely reaches 80% (snippet) and in the ChatArena ablation (alpha=0.15) 63% coverage, 85.8% agreement, relative API cost 2.85 vs GPT-4 N=5 at 5.0, i.e. cascade with N=1 costs 0.655 of GPT-4 N=1 while raising agreement 77.8 -> 85.2 (note: the lift comes from abstaining, so agreement is on accepted items only; coverage must always be reported next to it).

TRUST OR ESCALATE BASELINES AND CONFIDENCE FINDINGS (verified): confidence baselines were predictive probability and verbalized confidence; both over-confident for preference judging even with GPT-4-turbo (e.g. verbalized-confidence ECE 0.215 to 0.414 depending on judge vs 0.04 to 0.106 for Simulated Annotators; AUROC 0.55-0.63 vs 0.72-0.88). Their Simulated Annotators = agreement across N=5 K-shot prompted copies of the same model (ensemble of N, K<=5), i.e. essentially vote-agreement as confidence, and more annotators bought more coverage but cost scaled with N. Selection baselines they beat: Heuristic Selection (lambda=1-alpha assuming perfect calibration), Cascaded Heuristic Selection, and Point-Estimate Calibration (smallest lambda with empirical R_hat<=alpha on Dcal, no testing); all three had near-0% to ~57% guarantee success. Distribution shift: calibration assumes i.i.d. Dcal; they test disjoint-model splits (Table 9) and see small degradation only. Also they check that abstained items are the ones humans disagree on (inter-annotator agreement 0.815 abstained vs 0.902 accepted) while shallow features (length ratio, ROUGE-L) show no difference, a useful sanity check that the confidence is not a spurious proxy.

SEMANTIC AGREEMENT CASCADES (Soiffer, Kolawole, Smith, EMNLP 2025 Industry, 2509.21837, verified): deferral signal = mean pairwise similarity (BLEURT/SBERT/ROUGE) among outputs of several cheap models (cross-model ensemble, not repeated samples of one model); training-free, label-free, black-box. Evaluation protocol: quality at a fixed budget of 40% of the target model's FLOPs, and cost/latency needed to reach 98% of target quality; cost = sum of FLOPs over ALL ensemble members (parallel latency, summed cost). Deferral-curve metric AUC-DF with an explicit Random reference (expected AUC when deferring uniformly at random from the best base model). Results are modest and honest: Table 2 SQuAD .8353 semantic vs .8217 best token-level vs .8053 random; TriviaQA token-level (.7741) beats semantic (.7720); WMT FR-EN .7470 vs .7438 random (nearly flat); on XLSum NO strategy significantly beats random deferral and curves are flat. Lesson: when base quality gap or per-item variance is small, every confidence signal collapses to random, so always plot against random.

AGREEMENT IS NOT ACCURACY (Ding, arXiv 2607.08065, verified from full text of abstract/intro, Jul 2026): 53 runners x K=50 samples on GPQA Diamond and AIME (265k samples). Self-consistency C (share of K samples agreeing with the majority) is a positive but weak predictor of majority-correctness (Spearman 0.20 to 0.59), best for unsaturated mid-tier models and for allocating compute, worst for the most consistent frontier model: C>=0.8 on 77% of GPQA case entries and 48% of those were wrong. Exploratory check on claude-haiku-4.5 / sonnet-4.6 / opus-4.7 shows the same confident-error pattern, with confident errors recurring across providers. Methodology worth copying: hierarchical runner-clustered bootstrap, item-clustered resampling, and a marginal-preserving null. Consequence for AR3: repeated cheap passes at API default share the same prompt and the same bias, so unanimous-but-wrong is the key failure mode; you must measure the confident-wrong rate (accepted-and-wrong) directly, and it will be concentrated in the defect types Haiku systematically misses.

SELF-CONSISTENCY VS VERBALIZED CONFIDENCE (snippet-level; evidence is mixed, small-N): education grading study (2603.29559) found self-reported confidence better calibrated than self-consistency (ECE 0.166 vs 0.229) at ~1/5 the cost; GPQA/AIME audit found self-consistency had highest rank correlation with correctness (rho 0.31 vs 0.21 verbalized vs 0.19 P(True)) but verbalized gave the better risk-coverage curve and was unparseable on AIME (3/50), with wide CIs; DiNCo (2509.25532, ICLR 2026) says verbalized confidence is overconfident from suggestibility and that combining it with distractor-normalized consistency at 10 calls beats plain self-consistency at 100. Trust or Escalate (verified) found verbalized and token-probability confidence worse than agreement for judging. Takeaway: vote agreement is the right primary signal for your 'no logprobs via claude -p' setting, but a reviewer will ask for verbalized-confidence (ask Haiku for a 0-1 confidence in the JSON schema) as a one-call, 1/k-cost baseline, so include it.

SELECTIVE PREDICTION METRICS. Definitions (std): coverage c(t) = P(conf >= t); selective risk r(t) = P(error | conf >= t); risk-coverage curve = r vs c over thresholds; AURC = integral of selective risk over coverage (lower is better, mixes base error with ranking quality, so a worse model can have worse AURC even with a perfect confidence score). Oracle ranking (reject all errors first) gives the lowest AURC for a given model; random ranking gives constant risk equal to base error. E-AURC = AURC minus oracle AURC (excess, isolates ranking quality). AUROC of confidence for predicting failure (and AUPRC, ECE) judge the ranking/calibration separately. Traub et al., NeurIPS 2024 (2407.01032, snippet-level): AURC has flaws (not task-aligned, not interpretable, ignores what happens at a working point, weights low coverage heavily); propose AUGRC = area under the Generalized Risk-Coverage curve where the y-axis is P(accepted AND wrong) (rate of undetected failures, bounded [0, 1/2]), changed the ranking of 13 confidence scorers on 5 of 6 datasets; they criticize fixed-working-point evaluation. One 2026 preprint claims AUGRC is an affine function of AUROC at fixed accuracy (single source, verify before citing). Also: Zhou et al. propose Monte-Carlo plug-in estimators for finite-sample AURC (2410.15361, snippet-level).

ROUTING/CASCADE COST-QUALITY METRICS (snippet-level except where noted). RouteLLM (2406.18665): CPT(x%) = minimum fraction of calls that must go to the strong model to reach x% of strong-model quality (lower better; sources disagree whether x is a fraction of strong performance or an improvement over the weak baseline, so define it explicitly in your doc); APGR = average performance gap recovered, PGR(c) = (Q(c) - Q_weak) / (Q_strong - Q_weak), averaged over call budgets; reference = random router that sends the same fraction of calls to the strong model. RouterBench (2403.12031): oracle router (picks best model per query, cheapest on ties) as the ceiling, AIQ = normalized area under the cost-quality curve. LLMRouterBench (2601.07206): Pareto dominance over (accuracy, cost) and ParetoDist = distance to the frontier; reference points random, best single model, oracle; reports cost savings at fixed accuracy and gap-to-oracle. Semantic Agreement paper (verified): quality at fixed 40% budget and cost to reach 98% of target quality, with AUC-DF and a Random reference. AutoMix (2310.12963): IBC = incremental benefit per cost (quality gain of the mixed system over the small model divided by extra cost over the small model, normalized against always-large baseline slope), up to 57% to 86% IBC improvement depending on paper version, and the authors admit gains are sometimes negligible or negative where self-verification is uninformative.

WHAT THE LITERATURE SAYS ABOUT FAILURE MODES OF ROUTERS: 'Routing collapse' (Lai and Ye, 2602.03478, snippet-level): as budget grows many learned routers send nearly all traffic to the strongest model, while the oracle uses it on a small fraction, so a router must be compared to the cheap-model default and to the oracle, not just to always-strong. Cascade Routing (Dekoninck, Baader, Vechev, ICML 2025, 2410.10347, snippet-level): proves an optimal cascading strategy exists and states the quality estimator is the decisive factor, i.e. cascade results are mostly a statement about the estimator's calibration. Gupta et al. ICLR 2024 (2404.10136, snippet-level): Chow's rule on sequence probability has length bias (long outputs defer more, or short ones after normalization); learned token-level deferral rules beat sum/mean aggregation; no single quantile works across settings. For structured JSON verdicts from a critic this length bias matters less, but still check that escalation rate does not correlate with response length or number of defects flagged.

RISK CONTROL FOR THRESHOLDS: Learn then Test (Angelopoulos, Bates, Candes, Jordan, Lei, 2110.01052): pick the threshold by testing each candidate lambda as a hypothesis 'risk > alpha'; with probability >= 1-delta over the calibration draw the returned lambda-hat has risk <= alpha; fixed-sequence testing (scan from conservative end, stop at first failure) needs no multiplicity correction and does not need monotone risk (monotonicity only helps power). CALM (2207.07061) applies it to confidence-based early exit. Caveat reported in 2604.23333: validity does not imply efficiency, and if confidence is uncalibrated or non-monotone LTT picks conservative thresholds (low coverage). The guarantee is conditional on i.i.d. calibration/test and is on selective risk, not on end-to-end cost. Small-N evaluation: CLT error bars underestimate uncertainty below a few hundred items (ICML 2025 position paper, snippet-level); use paired bootstrap (resample items jointly across systems), exact McNemar on discordant pairs for binary outcomes, and clustered bootstrap when several rows share an item. A non-inferiority framing (lower CI bound of paired difference > -margin) is standard clinical-trial practice but I found no LLM-cascade source that uses it; I am suggesting it, not citing it.

UNVERIFIED/OUT OF SCOPE: I did not find a source defining an 'equal-budget' protocol for cascades explicitly (search said so); the common practice is (a) read both systems off the same cost axis and compare quality at equal cost, or cost at equal quality, with random-escalation-at-equal-escalation-rate as the null, and (b) report oracle escalation as the upper bound. I did not find a paper on evaluating autoresearch agents' own ledgers under mixed-model assignments; AR5 has no direct precedent in the cascade literature and its design must borrow from paired A/B evaluation instead.
recommendations: METRICS TO PRE-REGISTER FOR AR3 (define each in the AR3 doc): (1) escalation rate e = fraction of critic calls sent to Sonnet; (2) cost per item in token-weighted dollars including ALL cheap passes (k cheap calls always pay, plus Sonnet on escalated items), expressed as ratio to one Sonnet call; also report strong-call fraction separately because the claim mirrors claim 1's 'quarter of the verifier calls'; (3) quality vs two targets, kept separate: agreement with the Sonnet critic (consistency) and recall/precision against the PLANTED defects in AR2 (ground truth); (4) selective risk and coverage of the cheap tier alone (accepted-and-wrong rate = AUGRC-style undetected-failure rate, plus AURC/E-AURC and AUROC of agreement for predicting cheap error); (5) the full cost-quality curve over the threshold sweep (not one point), summarized by cost to reach 98% of Sonnet quality, quality at 25% strong-call budget, and an AIQ/APGR-style area; (6) calibration of agreement (reliability diagram, ECE) so the burn-in diagnostic has something to read.

BASELINES A REVIEWER WILL DEMAND (all on the SAME items, same seeds budgeting): cheap-only single pass (e=0); cheap-only majority/union of k passes with no escalation (this isolates whether escalation beats just voting more); strong-only single pass (e=1) and strong-only k passes; random escalation at the same escalation rate (average over >=200 random draws, report band); oracle escalation (escalate exactly the items where cheap is wrong versus the target; upper bound and shows headroom); verbalized-confidence escalation (ask Haiku for a 0-1 confidence in the schema, 1 call) as the cheap-signal rival; a learned scorer (FrugalGPT style: logistic regression on features such as agreement, number of flags, response length, defect type) cross-validated, since claim 1 says learned allocators never beat the threshold and AR3 should test the same on the critic; a length/flag-count-only escalation rule as a spurious-proxy control; and the Sonnet-vs-Sonnet self-agreement ceiling (two independent Sonnet passes against each other), because sampling is at API default and the 'strong critic' is itself noisy; a cascade cannot be asked to agree with Sonnet more than Sonnet agrees with itself.

HOW TO REPORT EQUAL BUDGET: pick budgets as fractions of the strong-only cost (e.g. 15%, 25%, 40%, 60%), set each method's threshold to hit that budget on the calibration split, then report quality on the test split with paired-bootstrap CIs for (method minus random-escalation) and (method minus strong-only); also report the reverse view (cost needed to reach 98% / 99% of strong quality). Show the oracle and random curves on the same plot, report the gap closed = (Q_method - Q_random) / (Q_oracle - Q_random) at each budget, and plot Pareto frontier with points for the cheap-only and strong-only endpoints. State the cost model explicitly (token-weighted, includes the ~1k token claude -p overhead per call, so k=3 cheap passes may cost more than they seem; Haiku vs Sonnet price ratio must be taken from the current price sheet, not assumed). Report wall time too since passes can run in parallel.

THRESHOLD AND LEAKAGE DISCIPLINE (the pitfalls): (a) never choose the threshold, k, or the 'burn-in diagnostic budget' on the items used to report results; split into burn-in/calibration and test, and split by SOURCE ENTRY (ledger entry or original artifact), not by defect variant, otherwise planted variants of one entry land on both sides; (b) the agreement signal must be label-free at deployment: label leakage happens if the planted-defect label or the Sonnet verdict is used to pick k or the agreement function, or if the diagnostic sees test items; the burn-in diagnostic is allowed to see labels only on the burn-in slice, then freeze budget and threshold before touching test; (c) point-estimate calibration is the documented failure (Trust or Escalate: guarantee success 0 to ~57%), so either use a binomial upper confidence bound with fixed-sequence scan (alpha, delta=0.1) or at minimum repeat the cal/test split >=1000 times and report the distribution of test risk and the fraction of splits meeting target; (d) do not tune the escalation rule while peeking at test curves; run a single pre-registered rule and treat anything else as exploratory; (e) selecting the best of several signals (agreement, verbalized, learned) on the test set is multiple comparisons, report all.

STATISTICAL POWER AND NOISE (AR3): AR2's item count is probably small (check /homes/rdubash/active-audit/avrl/runs/AR2/ before fixing alpha); with a few hundred items a 1-delta bound on a 15% risk with 40% coverage will be loose and LTT may select no threshold, so power-plan first: compute the Clopper-Pearson interval width at the expected n(lambda). Use paired bootstrap clustered by source entry, exact McNemar for binary agreement outcomes, and repeat the whole pipeline over several independent resamples of the API-default sampling noise (rerun the k cheap passes and the Sonnet pass at least 3 times per item or bootstrap the repeated draws) and report between-run variance. Treat a null as informative only with a stated non-inferiority margin (suggest, e.g., Sonnet-agreement drop <= 2 to 3 points, to be fixed before looking).

SPECIFIC AGREEMENT-SIGNAL CHECKS: (1) report the confident-wrong rate of the cheap tier (unanimous k passes and wrong versus planted ground truth), broken down by defect type, since Ding (2607.08065) shows agreement can be high with near-chance accuracy and confident errors recur across runs, so a cascade can pass on average and still miss one defect class entirely; (2) sweep k in {1,3,5} and report marginal gain, as Trust or Escalate saw coverage rise with N but cost scale linearly; (3) vote the structured fields, not free text (agreement on verdict + defect-type set; use Jaccard on flagged-defect sets if the critic returns lists); (4) verify agreement is not just a proxy for response length or number of flags (their abstained-vs-evaluated shallow-feature check); (5) because temperature is at API default, report the agreement distribution (histogram) so the threshold is not sitting on a degenerate mass at 1.0.

AR5 DESIGN CAUTIONS FROM THIS LITERATURE (inferences; no direct precedent found): the evaluation analogue of 'relativistic' scoring is paired variant-vs-variant comparison from an identical starting state; report per-experiment paired outcomes against the day-one verdicts with paired bootstrap, not just arm totals. One 8 hour run per arm is n=1, so state it as a case study or replicate at least twice per arm with different seeds and show the spread; ledger error rate needs a blinded audit (auditor does not see which arm wrote the entry) and a pre-specified error taxonomy. Ground-truth circularity: the original day-one verdicts were produced by the all-Sonnet loop, so the all-Sonnet arm is partly graded against itself; mitigate by auditing disputed verdicts against the raw run artifacts/metrics, not against the old ledger text, and by reporting the arm's disagreement with day one separately from its error rate. Report cost per arm broken down by role, experiments-to-verdict as time-to-first-correct-verdict plus a censored survival style view (some arms may never reach a verdict in 8 h), and wall time with the lab-pool contention noted (shared NFS, different A4000 machines make wall time noisy; pin each arm to comparable hosts or interleave).

WHAT TO CITE IN THE ZUBIN-FACING WRITE-UP: FrugalGPT and Trust or Escalate as the two anchors (Trust or Escalate is the closest methodological template: agreement-based confidence, fixed-sequence-tested threshold, cascade, guarantee-success-rate reporting); Semantic Agreement cascades for label-free agreement with the honest 'nothing beats random on XLSum' result; Traub et al. for AUGRC; RouteLLM CPT/APGR plus RouterBench oracle for the equal-budget and oracle conventions; Ding 2607.08065 as the explicit warning that agreement is a conditional proxy. This also fits his drift worry: a frozen threshold is a deployment hazard, so propose a rolling re-audit (small random audit slice of cheap-accepted items judged by Sonnet each night) to estimate the accepted-and-wrong rate and trigger recalibration; this audit slice is also the cheap online estimate of undetected failures.

SUGGESTED HEADLINE CLAIM FORMS THAT SURVIVE REVIEW: 'At alpha = X (accepted-and-wrong rate vs planted truth) with delta = 0.1, the cheap-first cascade achieved coverage C and used S% of Sonnet calls, in G% of 1000 cal/test splits, versus random escalation at equal S achieving risk R_rand'; avoid 'matches Sonnet' without the noise ceiling and CI; avoid reporting agreement on accepted items without coverage; avoid reporting a single threshold.

ZUBIN TALK FACTS (StartupHub https://www.startuphub.ai/news/weights-biases-made-its-agent-improve-itself , sean-weldon https://www.sean-weldon.com/blog/2026-09-29-how-we-built-an-agent-that-improves-itself-zubin-aysola-weights-biases , BigGo https://finance.biggo.com/news/f34ddf874012b8cc): title 'How We Built an Agent That Improves Itself', AI Engineer World's Fair 2026, Zubin is a Senior SWE on Weave. Agent is called ARIA (StartupHub misspells 'Arya'); GA week of Sept 21 2026 after public preview June 29 2026. Core claim: a tight flywheel between production traces and an offline simulation running byte-identical agent code. Weave logs prod and offline traces in the same format; a four-hour sync job copies prod code into the research sandbox 'so hill climbing never drifts'. Offline corpus is 886 YAML tasks (starting conditions, user configs, ending conditions), organized by difficulty level and reviewed by product teams for relevance; three simulation modalities: plain instruction, persona-based multi-turn user simulation, direct replay of production traces. Production failures AND successes become tasks ('becomes a task for our agent framework'; BigGo calls the principle WBAF = Weights & Biases Agent Factory, but no primary source defines it, and a web search for 'W&B Agent Factory' found nothing, so the user-supplied 'Agent Factory' term is unverified externally). Sandbox DAG: YAML config, hydrate, set up env, rehydrate (hot-patch runtime config), run agent, score; environments are expensive (full ML training logs, simulated GPU runs) and torn down after parallel runs. Nightly CI over 7 weeks benchmarks production plus candidate variants, 'hovering around 66%' on some task families/classes (not all, not named, no baseline given). CI broke the night before and ARIA self-repaired. Live demo: ARIA turned a real prod error (missed weave.log SDK call in sandbox) into a regression task, wrote a fix as a prompt edit to an existing skill, re-ran against prod version. Stated limits: simulation expensive and slow; 'the gap between offline scores and live behavior still needs manual review'; a team member audited drift between offline evals and production; team spent a full day on 'evaluation health and drift'. He says he spends most of his time on scoring robustness. Other quotes: 'It's just better to run more experiments than fewer' (parallel YAML variants); 'It's really easy to go auto mode for some of these tasks' (caution). He directs Claude for code, 'focuses on guardrails'; ARIA trains on H200s on CoreWeave and runs auto-research on Karpathy's nanochat inside Weave.

WHAT 'RELATIVISTIC SCORING' MEANS (best available): per sean-weldon, 'compares variant behaviors against one another' with example 'whether a variant asks clarifying questions or proceeds without them'; BigGo: compares variants against each other, one variant asks the user questions and one does not, to see which behaves better, 'traditional from a reinforcement learning standpoint' (i.e. preference/pairwise ranking, reward-model style, not absolute correctness). Contrast: 'normative' = pass/fail against a task's ending conditions. BigGo frames nightly CI numbers plus relativistic scoring as the instrument to tell 'compounding gains' from 'silent drift' (the open question in the talk; drift = offline-optimized variant 'diverges silently from what is actually deployed'). No source gives a formula, judge, or aggregation (Elo, win rate, etc.). Inference for AR3/AR5: expect variant-vs-variant, same-task, paired comparison on identical starting state and identical task set, reported as win/tie/loss or delta over time, rather than absolute scores. The AR5 design (identical start, different role-model assignments, compared pairwise on same ledger verdicts) maps naturally onto this.

ARIA PRODUCT CLAIMS (CoreWeave blog https://www.coreweave.com/blog/introducing-coreweave-aria-ai-research-and-iteration-agent , press release https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260629000491/en/CoreWeave-ARIA-Launches-as-an-AI-Research-and-Iteration-Agent-with-autonomous-research-and-collaborative-intelligence , product page https://wandb.ai/site/agent/): ARIA = AI Research and Iteration Agent, a coding agent inside W&B that forms hypotheses, writes configs, launches runs via W&B Launch, evaluates against a baseline, drafts a W&B Report, proposes next steps. Trust claims are traceability only ('every run tracked, every decision visible in the conversation', 'reports exactly where it looked and what it ruled out'). Blog publishes NO accuracy, error-rate, hallucination, or statistical-test numbers; no approval-gating description; roadmap includes bring-your-own API keys, custom skills/MCP, persistent memory. So the vendor audience is used to anecdotal/demo evidence on ARIA itself and a gap exists where an audited error rate would stand out. Weave evals (https://site.wandb.ai/evaluations) = dataset + scorers, side-by-side comparison, versioned code/datasets/scorers, online evals on live traces.

KARPATHY AUTORESEARCH (secondary: https://lilting.ch/en/articles/karpathy-autoresearch-autonomous-ml-agent , https://themenonlab.blog/blog/karpathy-autoresearch-autonomous-ml-experiments , VESSL https://vessl.ai/en/blog/dont-tie-gpu-to-agent): fixed 5-minute training budget per experiment, single scalar val_bpb (vocab-size independent so architecture/tokenizer changes are comparable), keep-or-revert on the metric; ~12 experiments/hour ideal, ~100 per 8 h night; VESSL measured ~7/h sequential in cloud (startup overhead). Ground truth here is trivial because the objective is a verifiable scalar; the credibility risk is noise and selection, not label correctness. Reported metrics: experiments/hour, val_bpb delta, wall time, dollars.

SELECTION AND NOISE ARE THE CREDIBILITY ATTACK ON LIVE LOOPS: NeurIPS 2026 'Separating Real Improvements from Lucky Runs in Autonomous ML Research' (https://neurips.cc/virtual/2026/157611): 60-seed noise measurement on nanoGPT; best-of-32 of identical runs yields apparent +0.00544 val_bpb 'entirely by selection' (~2.7x the pre-registered delta 0.002); 24-candidate frozen bank incl. 9 exact nulls; agent-found large gains (~0.014 val_bpb) confirmed on sealed held-out seeds, of 15 non-null candidates 8 replicated, 3 failed, 4 inconclusive even after 24-33 sealed evals; 749 runs. Rehearse (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.27687, via AutoSOTA logs): fraction of agent changes that improve falls from 70% early to 43% by iteration 6+, with shrinking gains. Also https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07150v2 style guidance: multiple runs per task, power analysis, pass@k/pass^k; paired-seed designs tighten CIs. Single-seed LLM results swing 5-15 pts (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.07086). Implication: a 4-arm, 8-hour, one-seed AR5 is a pilot, not a result, unless noise is measured (e.g. repeat the all-Sonnet arm or run null/replay controls).

AI SCIENTIST V2 (Sakana; https://huggingface.co/papers/2504.08066.md , https://github.com/sakanaai/ai-scientist-v2): agentic tree search with experiment manager, no human templates; 3 fully autonomous manuscripts to an ICLR workshop, 1 passed review (avg 6.33, above ~55% of human submissions), then withdrawn; ground truth = human peer review score, i.e. an external noisy judge. Cost per paper only from third-party blogs (~$15-25, unverified; e.g. https://www.danilchenko.dev/posts/2026-04-06-ai-scientist-v2-first-peer-reviewed-ai-paper/). Independent audit of v1 (Beel, Kan, Baumgart https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14297): 5 of 12 proposed experiments (42%) failed from coding errors, some finished runs gave misleading results, an 'energy efficiency' experiment reported accuracy gains at higher compute, novelty judgments wrong (called micro-batching SGD novel), hallucinated numbers in manuscripts. This is the template for an 'independent audit of the system's own claims' and the closest precedent to the AR5 independently audited ledger error rate.

EVOLVE-STYLE SYSTEMS (ShinkaEvolve https://arxiv.org/html/2509.19349v1 , https://sakana.ai/shinka-evolve/ ; AlphaEvolve harness https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/alphaevolve/developer-guide/logical-architecture ; OpenEvolve cascade example https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.14555): headline metric is sample efficiency (samples/generations to reach a verifiable score), e.g. circle packing beats AlphaEvolve in <150 evaluations (sum of radii 2.635983 under relaxed verifier), ALE-Bench 50 gens ~2.3% avg gain over ALE-Agent, AIME 75 gens with 3 independent runs per candidate. Shinka reports NO dollar or token cost (it admits API cost is a barrier) and its LLM-ensemble ablation is shown only in a figure: a UCB1 bandit over LLMs, rewarded on RELATIVE improvement over parent, beats a single LLM (GPT-5-nano) and a fixed ensemble. This is direct precedent for per-role/per-model routing in a loop, and also shows the gap: no cost accounting. Ground truth = deterministic programmatic evaluator. AlphaEvolve/OpenEvolve use an evaluation CASCADE (cheap syntax/import gate, then small-fraction calibration gate with ~30-40% pass, then full held-out eval) which is a structural analogue of the AR3 cheap-then-strong critic cascade. Known framework hazard: OpenEvolve apply_diff does not enforce EVOLVE-BLOCK boundaries (Issue #281), so mutators can edit the evaluator (reward hacking surface). Google-published AlphaEvolve gains are vendor examples, not independent.

BENCHMARKS WITH OPEN-ENDED GROUND TRUTH: MLE-bench (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.07095) uses 75 Kaggle comps; ground truth = leaderboard-derived medal thresholds (bronze/silver/gold scaled by team count); headline = any-medal rate, plus valid-submission rate, pass@k over several attempts and compute/time budget (24h, one A10 in the original); third-party rates like 73.3% any-medal for Claude Code are not leaderboard-comparable (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.25955). PaperBench (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.01848 , https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/starace25a.html): 20 ICML 2024 papers, 8,316 gradable leaf criteria in author-co-developed rubric trees, weighted-average Replication Score, LLM judge validated against human grading; best agent ~21% vs human PhD ~22-41% depending on source. Pattern: open-ended research gets ground truth by (a) a programmatic scalar, (b) external leaderboard thresholds, (c) human-co-developed rubrics graded by a validated LLM judge, or (d) human peer review. For AR5 the analog is the original campaign's day-one verdicts (a frozen answer key), which is legitimate but is itself produced by the same loop family, so it should be disclosed as a reference not an oracle.

SCALING AGENT SYSTEMS (https://research.google/blog/towards-a-science-of-scaling-agent-systems-when-and-why-agent-systems-work/ , https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.08296): 180 configurations across 5 architectures (single, independent, centralized, decentralized, hybrid) and model families; metrics are task success, cost/token overhead, and coordination metrics incl. error amplification (independent agents 17.2x, centralized 4.4x, with orchestrator acting as validation bottleneck); centralized +80.9% on parallelizable tasks but all multi-agent variants -39% to -70% on sequential tasks; diminishing/negative returns once single-agent baseline exceeds ~45%; predictive model R2=0.513, picks best strategy on 87% of held-out configs. Relevance: AR5 role-assignment arms are a sequential pipeline (planner, runner, analyst, critic), so expect errors to propagate downstream and report error amplification explicitly (a planted/early bad verdict's downstream contamination), and the ~45% saturation point suggests a strong critic's marginal value is largest where cheap roles err.

2026 ROUTING BY ROLE: evidence is mostly vendor/blog and thin. Planner-strong/executor-cheap pattern: Plan-and-Act (ICML 2025), MinionS, vendor claim of ~4x execution-side savings (https://www.morphllm.com/multi-agent-model-routing , unverified); GraphPlanner (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.23626) casts routing as sequential choice of agent role per step with cost/accuracy per edge; guides at https://augmentcode.com/guides/ai-model-routing-guide and https://ai.engineer/talks/QHBjufYK8TA-state-model-routing-nvidia-cognition-openrouter ; hidden cost warning that delegation carries orchestrator context so multi-agent can cost more than one scoped agent (https://activewizards.com/blog/crewai-cost-control-token-budgets-model-routing-and-crew-composition-economics/). I found no independent, audited, live-loop comparison of role-wise model assignment with cost, time, and error rates. That is the open slot AR5 would fill, but also means there is no accepted protocol to cite.

METRICS THESE SYSTEMS REPORT (synthesis): throughput (experiments/hour, time-to-GPT-2, samples-to-target); outcome (val_bpb delta, medal rate, replication score, workshop review score, nightly pass rate ~66%); cost (rarely: $5 VESSL run, ~$15-25/paper third-party; Shinka and ARIA publish none); error rates (almost only from independent audits: Beel 42% failed experiments; replication rates 8 of 15 in NeurIPS selection paper; Rehearse improvement-rate decay 70% to 43%); reliability (pass@k, multiple seeds, error amplification). Ground-truth handling is the weak spot everywhere except programmatic-scalar tasks.

AUDIENCE FIT: Zubin's own talk concedes four things an AR5 report can speak to directly: (1) offline vs live gap needs manual review, (2) drift between eval and prod must be audited, (3) CI is noisy and his headline is a ~66% band without baseline, (4) relativistic scoring is variant-vs-variant. A rigorous, paired, cost-accounted, independently audited comparison on the lab pool would address (1)-(4) and is more rigorous than anything he published, but only if variance is measured.

findings: SEARCH COVERAGE: 9 WebSearch calls + 5 WebFetch (Miller PDF/HTML, 3 arXiv abs pages; two abs pages gave only abstracts). All code below was run and verified in /homes/rdubash/yes/bin/python (scipy 1.15.3, statsmodels 0.14.6; system python3 has no scipy; test script /tmp/claude-22830/-homes-rdubash/2d8b70a3-2fb9-42a6-aac4-20bd12ab9c6d/scratchpad/t.py). Caveat: several cited 2026 arXiv papers are preprints seen via abstract/snippet only; I did not read their full text.

PAIRED TWO-CLASSIFIER TEST (AR3 critic-vs-critic, AR5 arm-vs-arm on the same ledger verdicts). Build the 2x2 on identical items: n10 = A right, B wrong; n01 = A wrong, B right. Only discordant pairs carry information. Dietterich (1998, via secondary summary) says McNemar is the right test when each algorithm can only be run once on one test set. For small k = n10+n01 (rule of thumb k<25) use the EXACT conditional test, which is a binomial test on n10 given k with p=0.5. The standard exact test is conservative; Fagerland, Lydersen, Laake (2013, BMC Med Res Methodol 13:91) recommend the MID-P exact McNemar as the best default (better type I error and power than exact or asymptotic). Verified code: p_exact = scipy.stats.binomtest(min(n10,n01), k, 0.5).pvalue ; p_mid = p_exact - scipy.stats.binom.pmf(min(n10,n01), k, 0.5). statsmodels.stats.contingency_tables.mcnemar(table, exact=True).pvalue returns the exact (not mid-p) value (matched 0.21875 in my test). Worked example: 60 items, n10=5, n01=1 gives exact p=0.219, mid-p=0.125, i.e. 6 discordant pairs cannot resolve anything.

PAIRED BOOTSTRAP: resample ITEMS (not calls) with replacement, recompute the paired statistic each time; use for non-accuracy metrics (kappa, cost-adjusted score, cascade metrics). Code: scipy.stats.bootstrap((d,), np.mean, confidence_level=0.95, method='percentile' or 'BCa', n_resamples=9999, random_state=0) where d = a_i - b_i per item. WARNING (observed): on a discrete d with few nonzero entries BCa/percentile intervals degenerate (got [0.0, 0.15] for 6 discordant pairs of 60), so at small n prefer the exact/mid-p McNemar for the p-value and use the bootstrap only as a secondary interval. Sign-flip permutation on d (scipy.stats.permutation_test((d,), lambda x,axis: np.mean(x,axis=axis), permutation_type='samples', n_resamples=9999)) gave 0.2188, essentially the exact McNemar p, so it is an equivalent cross-check (the abeval package uses it as primary). A 2026 arXiv paper (2605.30315) calibrates McNemar variants against a paired bootstrap at n=500 and recommends the bootstrap only when no closed-form variance exists; it found no small-n comparison, so none exists in what I read. For continuous paired scores with n<~10 use scipy.stats.wilcoxon (exact for n<=50 w/o ties) or the sign test.

PAIRED-DIFFERENCE SE AND CLUSTERING (Miller 2024, arXiv 2411.00640, Anthropic): SE_CLT = sqrt( (1/(n-1)) sum (s_i - sbar)^2 / n ); Bernoulli SE = sqrt(sbar(1-sbar)/n); CI95 = sbar +/- 1.96 SE. Paired: SE_{A-B} = sqrt(Var(s_A - s_B)/n) = sqrt(SE_A^2 + SE_B^2 - 2 SE_A SE_B Corr(s_A,s_B)); unpaired would be sqrt(SE_A^2+SE_B^2), so pairing helps whenever scores correlate positively. Clustered SE is needed when items share a source (up to 3x larger than naive on DROP, RACE-H, MGSM). Analogue for us: AR5 experiments from the same campaign or planted defects from the same base experiment are clusters; use cluster-robust SE or a cluster bootstrap (resample base experiments, keep their children together). Power (Eq. 9): n = (z_{a/2}+z_b)^2 (omega^2 + sigma_A^2/K_A + sigma_B^2/K_B)/delta^2, with omega^2 = Var(x_A)+Var(x_B)-2Cov(x_A,x_B); Miller says new evals should have >=1000 questions for good signalling ability (we will be far below that, so report MDE rather than claiming equivalence). Accuracy-specific McNemar power (Connor 1987): n = [ z_{a/2} sqrt(psi) + z_b sqrt(psi - delta^2) ]^2 / delta^2, psi = P(discordant). Example: psi=0.20, delta=0.10, alpha=.05, power=.8 gives n~154 items.

RESOLUTION DIAGNOSTIC (arXiv 2605.30315, 2026): treat a paired comparison as a test, invert it to the required sample size N*, and report the resolution ratio q = N/N* per pair; 11 of 40 Open LLM Leaderboard v1 pairs and 4/9 MMLU-Pro top-10 adjacent pairs fail (alpha,power)=(0.05,0.8), 6/9 once subject clustering is counted. It also warns that the unpaired Cohen's h shortcut with a (1-rho) adjustment understates N* about 2x for close comparisons. This is directly relevant: report q for every AR3/AR5 contrast and state 'unresolved' when q<1 instead of reading a null as equivalence.

RATE INTERVALS: statsmodels.stats.proportion.proportion_confint(count, nobs, alpha=0.05, method=...). Default method is 'normal' (Wald), which is bad at small n or near 0/1, so ALWAYS pass method explicitly. 'wilson' = Wilson score (near-nominal coverage even at small n; Brown, Cai, DasGupta 2001); 'beta' = Clopper-Pearson (exact, guaranteed >= nominal coverage but wider; at count 0 or n the statsmodels docs say coverage is only 1-alpha/2 for 'beta'); 'jeffreys' and 'agresti_coull' also available. Verified: 5/12 -> Wilson (0.193, 0.680), CP (0.152, 0.723). Policy: Wilson as the headline interval for escalation rate, error rate, and agreement rate; Clopper-Pearson when the claim is a guarantee (e.g. 'critic missed 0 of 12 planted defects': one-sided 95% CP upper bound = 1 - 0.05^(1/n), roughly 3/n, 22% at n=12). For a rate against a fixed target use scipy.stats.binomtest(k, n, p0, alternative=...).

COST-QUALITY CURVES. No standard significance test for comparing whole curves exists in the literature I found; the practice is (a) scalar summaries: RouterBench AIQ (normalized area under the route-quality curve, arXiv 2403.12031), nAUC (MMR-Bench), AUC-DF area under deferral curve (Google Research, 'Language Model Cascades: Token-level uncertainty and beyond'), LLMRouterBench normalized L1 distance to the Pareto frontier (arXiv 2601.07206) with dominance = at least equal accuracy and no higher cost, at least one strict; VL-RouterBench replaces the non-decreasing convex hull with a parametric saturation curve; and (b) fixed-budget or fixed-quality operating-point comparisons with a paired bootstrap. The closest template to AR3: arXiv 2604.19781 bootstraps the paired kappa difference (cascade minus large-model-alone) over the same decisions with 10k resamples, picks the cheapest Pareto-optimal threshold within 0.02 kappa of the large model, and reports the CI (Claude: -0.017, 95% CI [-0.039, +0.005]). Theory: Bouchard arXiv 2605.06350 characterizes two-model threshold cascades and notes cost is limited by the structural cost of always paying the cheap model first (for AR3 this means 3 cheap passes are paid on every item, count them).

CASCADE-SPECIFIC ANALYSIS PLAN (my synthesis from the above). Cost axis = strong-critic calls per item (plus Haiku passes weighted by price ratio, e.g. use measured USD from the --output-format json cost field). Quality = agreement with ground truth (planted defect labels) in AR3. Procedure: (1) split items into burn-in (threshold selection, diagnose.py budget choice) and held-out test; never tune on test. (2) Sweep the agreement threshold t over {2/3, 3/3 agreement among 3 passes, or finer if more passes}; each t gives an (escalation rate, accuracy) point. (3) Paired item bootstrap (cluster bootstrap by base experiment): for each resample recompute the whole cascade at the burn-in-chosen t, collect accuracy(cascade) - accuracy(strong-only) and calls(cascade)/calls(strong-only); report percentile CIs for both. (4) Non-inferiority claim 'matches': pre-register margin M (e.g. 0.05 absolute accuracy or kappa 0.02-0.05), claim non-inferior only if the upper end of the one-sided 95% (or two-sided 90%) paired CI for (strong - cascade) is < M; this is TOST logic. With n of tens of items M this tight is unreachable, so state the MDE and q instead. (5) Also report the two baselines that bracket the curve: always-Haiku (0 strong calls) and random escalation at the same rate (the curve a useless confidence signal would trace); the claim 'agreement beats random' is a paired comparison at matched escalation rate.

MULTIPLE COMPARISONS for a handful of pre-registered reads: statsmodels.stats.multitest.multipletests(pvals, alpha=0.05, method='holm') returns (reject, p_corrected, alphacSidak, alphacBonf). The function DEFAULT is method='hs' (Holm-Sidak), so pass 'holm' explicitly; verified on [0.01,0.04,0.03] -> adjusted [0.03,0.06,0.06], reject [T,F,F]. Holm controls FWER, is uniformly more powerful than Bonferroni, and needs no independence assumption. Pre-registration papers recommend a primary confirmatory family with Holm when more than one test is included (arXiv 2507.04491); everything outside the family is labelled exploratory with unadjusted p and no claim. Use 'fdr_bh' only for a large exploratory set. For AR5 with 4 arms there are 3 contrasts against the all-Sonnet reference (Haiku-roles+Sonnet-critic, all-Haiku, Haiku+cascade): that is the confirmatory family, m=3, Holm. All-pairs (6) is exploratory.

SEED / REPEAT VARIANCE IN LLM EVALS (2024-2026): (1) Miller 2411.00640: total variance = Var(conditional mean over questions) + E[sigma_i^2]; resampling each question K times gives variance factor roughly (1+2/K)/3 in his binary uniform example (K=2 removes 1/3 of variance, K=4 removes 1/2, K=6 removes 5/9, limit 2/3); diminishing once E[sigma^2]/K << Var(x); compute the SE from per-question means over K, NOT pooled over K*N answers; do not lower temperature to cut variance (it shifts variance into the conditional-mean term or adds bias). (2) arXiv 2512.21326 'Measuring all the noises of LLM Evals': decomposes total noise (law of total variance) into prediction noise (same question, different answer) and data noise (which questions); paired prediction noise is usually LARGER than paired data noise, so averaging repeats raises power; total noise is fairly stable across model pairs; also argues a single error bar per model from a fixed-baseline paired scheme is not generally meaningful. (3) Madaan et al. arXiv 2406.10229 (NeurIPS 2024 workshop): 280+ models, 10 runs differing only in init seed; recommends measuring seed variance explicitly and that item-response-theory style tricks did not reduce it. (4) 'A Sober Look at Progress in LM Reasoning' arXiv 2504.07086: 20 seeds, 9 models, Pass@1 swings up to ~15 points on AIME'24 and 13 on AMC'23 purely from seed on small sets. (5) 'Evaluation is All You Need' arXiv 2506.04734: repeated each sample 16 times and 16 seeds as a cost trade-off, variation exceeded expectations. (6) Signal and Noise arXiv 2508.13144: more checkpoints give a less biased noise estimate. (7) arXiv 2503.07329: two fine-tuning seeds with identical 60% accuracy agreed on only 20% of predictions, and a review found 24 ACL papers using a single fixed seed. NO source gives a universal minimum seed count; defensible practice from these: >=3 repeats as the floor, 5 typical (a 2026 benchmark paper used 5 and flagged it as small), 10 to 20 when n_items is small or the claim is about a small delta. Relevance: your AR2 numbers and the 3-pass agreement signal in AR3 are exactly 'prediction noise at K=3' so cite 2512.21326.

SMALL-NUMBER-OF-SEEDS REPORTING FACTS (statistics): with S<5 repeats an SD or SE is itself very noisy (the CI for sigma from S=3 is roughly [0.52, 6.3] x s, from chi-square with 2 df), so show every per-seed value and the min-max range, not just mean +/- SE. Compute the t-based CI on seed means with scipy.stats.t.ppf(0.975, S-1) (S=3 gives 4.30, S=5 gives 2.78) rather than 1.96. Keep the SAME items across seeds and across arms so that paired differences are computed per seed and per item. Treat items nested in seeds correctly: per-item mean over K repeats first, then paired SE over items (Miller).

PRE-REGISTRATION FOR LLM EVALS (2026 preprints, none peer reviewed): arXiv 2606.11217 'Preregistration for Experiments with AI Agents' proposes a template aimed at researcher degrees of freedom (model selection, prompt wording, settings, outcome-contingent redesign) that are 'easy to exploit and hard to detect' because iteration is cheap; I could read only the abstract. arXiv 2606.27687 (Thomas, Gligoric, Shah, CMU) 'Mitigating LLM-based p-Hacking by Preregistering for the Next LLM': commit the protocol before a not-yet-released model exists, so configs cannot be hacked against it; across 20 models, 4 providers, 11 configs it would have blocked transfer of a p-hack in ~73% of cases (so a filter, not a fix); it asks to name eligible model families, inclusion thresholds, and what happens when a new family appears. arXiv 2507.04491 lists required components: prompt variations, model + version + temperature, analysis plan incl. robustness checks, boundary conditions of claims, multiplicity plan (Holm), judge model/prompt/version and disagreement or refusal handling, exclusion rules for refusals and malformed output, and a development-history disclosure (how many prompt iterations, which models were tried, whether preliminary results shaped hypotheses). Examples: an OSF prereg with foreknowledge statement and a Cohen's kappa >= 0.7 target for LLM-as-judge validation where the unmet kappa target was reported as a deviation; a physics-literacy study (arXiv 2607.00276) that froze verbatim prompts and judging scripts in one file before generating production data.

PRIOR-WORK FRAMING FOR ZUBIN: his 'relativistic' variant-vs-variant scoring is the paired comparison above (Miller Eq. 7 and McNemar); his silent-drift worry maps to 'unresolved pair' reporting (q = N/N*) and to repeated-seed noise floors (prediction noise): a nightly delta smaller than the measured paired noise floor should not be called a gain or a regression. A natural pitch line: AR3/AR5 produce an explicit noise floor and MDE, which his 886-task offline eval could adopt as the threshold for flagging drift.
recommendations: AR3 TEST BATTERY (pre-register verbatim). Unit = critic decision on one planted-defect item (or one real ledger entry with known verdict). Primary read P1: paired contrast, cascade vs strong-only, on correctness vs ground truth, via mid-p exact McNemar (scipy.stats.binomtest on n10 given k, minus binom.pmf of the observed count) AND report n10, n01, k. Primary read P2: strong-call fraction = strong_calls_cascade / strong_calls_strong_only with Wilson CI (proportion_confint(method='wilson')). Secondary: cost in USD from JSON output, paired item-cluster bootstrap CI. Confirmatory family = {P1, P2-below-threshold test via scipy.stats.binomtest(k, n, p0=0.5, alternative='less')} plus any third read, corrected with multipletests(method='holm'); everything else exploratory. Claim wording by outcome: if the paired CI for (strong - cascade) upper end < M then 'non-inferior within M at X% strong calls'; if k is too small to resolve (q<1) then 'unresolved, MDE = ...'; never 'matches' from a nonsignificant McNemar.

AR3 SIZING BEFORE RUNNING: pick expected discordance psi (from AR2 results, strong vs Haiku disagreement rate) and target delta, compute n = [1.96 sqrt(psi) + 0.84 sqrt(psi - delta^2)]^2 / delta^2 (Connor). Example psi=0.2, delta=0.10 needs ~154 items; psi=0.1, delta=0.05 needs ~ 4*154-ish scale, so if available items are fewer than the requirement, pre-register an MDE statement up front and treat AR3 as an estimate with an interval, not a test. Use the burn-in split (diagnose.py picks the budget) on a disjoint subset from the test set, fix the split by a seeded hash of the item id, and commit the split file.

AR3 REPEATS: K=3 Haiku passes per item is the agreement signal; additionally run the strong critic at least twice per item on a subset to measure the strong critic's own prediction noise, since the 'ground truth' ceiling is bounded by it (Miller: compute per-item mean over K then paired SE over items, never pooled SE over K*N). Report agreement rate, accuracy conditioned on unanimous vs split votes (Wilson CI each), and the monotone curve accuracy vs escalation rate against a random-escalation baseline at matched rate. Note that sampling is at API default temperature so passes are not independent of the model's systematic bias: unanimous-wrong cases are the key failure count to report (Clopper-Pearson if zero).

AR5 SIZING AND DESIGN: 4 arms, from an identical starting state, the original campaign's day-one verdicts as ground truth. Unit for verdict comparison = each pre-registered hypothesis or experiment verdict (pass/fail/inconclusive); the number of verdicts reachable in ~8 h is probably <20 per arm, so expect q<<1 for any accuracy contrast and plan to say so. scores.notes: Strongest: mechanical pool from the whole ledger (55-70 entries), entry-key by header hash, entry-level clustering, prevalence weighting, human blind adjudication of controls, IUT reads, analytic random baseline, 1000-split stability, noise floor/MDE/q. Flaws: (1) adjudication pile defined as controls flagged by ANY pass of EITHER model would be nearly every control (Haiku any-of-5 FA is high), so the '10-15 min of Rustom' estimate is wrong; (2) plant rule 'new value occurs nowhere in the entry' contradicts N-stale (value copied from the same table column); (3) the pool assertion 'no paragraph matches critic|corrected verdict|review note' fails on the 10 as-is entries (E06, L9d, L10a mention 'critic'), needs a hand whitelist; (4) natural probes 'left unstripped' would hand the critic the answer (original critic note is in the text), must be stripped like controls; (5) R3 bound 0.40 is looser than the 'quarter' it mirrors; (6) K3 and the 200-draw random band are extra complexity; (7) smoke run on pool entries should use excluded entries; (8) G1 at 0.06 barely clears the 0.05 NI margin, so NI could be satisfied by all-Haiku (needs the explicit all-Haiku NI check); (9) timeline is tight and the human step sits on the critical path.

Best Zubin framing (operating card: $/1000 checks, undetected-defect rate by kind, A/A noise floor, burn-in recipe reliability, rolling-audit drill, AR2 re-derivation) and good mechanics (queue order H1-3,S1,S2 then H4,H5,S3; 20 shuffle seeds for diagnose ties; q_ok feature; Sonnet-free hard cost stop; fixed-sequence CP variant; burn-in size curve). Excluded or unfair elements: (1) Sonnet pre-screen plus Sonnet adjudicator relabels controls and a Sonnet plant-validity gate: circular, favors Sonnet (declared but still biases the primary comparison); (2) prompt arms A/B/C selected on 6 dev sources (42 items) by Sonnet balanced error: noise-level selection, burns sources, arm A is the priming AR2 prompt, selection rule favors the strong tier; (3) Holm applied to a conjunction of three required reads (IUT needs no correction, Holm only loses power); (4) DIR direction-swap plants are not mechanically verifiable as defects; (5) choosing k in {3,5} by dollar cost adds a fork and k=5 dollar cost makes the claim near-vacuous; (6) the cross-draw rule (Sonnet pass 1 reference, passes 2-3 for outcomes) is unnecessary for truth-based quality and costs a pass; (7) C3 mixes a call bound (0.30) with a dollar bound (0.75) into the pass condition; (8) ~5900 calls plus dev/pre-screen/adjudication calls is not feasible in 3h with unknown rate limits; (9) bundles an AR2 ledger erratum that needs Rustom's go-ahead.

Cheapest and most feasible (~$12, ~1300 calls) with good engineering: pilot on excluded entries, hard cost stop, randomized (t,p) threshold with analytic tie handling, replay unit tests (b=0 equals Haiku vote, b=1 equals Sonnet, random midpoint), cross-check of diagnose residual against replay, Sonnet self-agreement ceiling. But underpowered by construction: hardcoded 42-entry pool minus Sonnet-adjudicated drops (~37 entries, ~25 test entries), only 3 plants per entry, burn-in of ~12 entries by sha1 mod 3 (variable size), so P2 non-inferiority is hopeless. Excluded or unfair: (1) dropping whole entries when Sonnet flags 2 of 3 passes, adjudicated by the implementing agent, is circular and favors Sonnet; (2) Holm over the PASS conjunction; (3) PASS clause 'b* at most 0.5' conflicts with e below 0.35; (4) body-only verdict flips with no header; (5) $25 cap too low once volume is raised; (6) skips the prevalence/kind-macro detail and the human adjudication of controls; (7) cluster/kind guards thinner (no natural-probe stripping detail, no extra ledger sections).

ar3.spec:
AR3 SPEC (judge-synthesized; winner = Design 0, with grafts from Designs 1 and 2). Implement without further questions. Python: test imports first; use /homes/rdubash/active-audit/.venv/bin/python for anything importing avrl_router.diagnose (pandas, pyarrow, sklearn), cwd /homes/rdubash/active-audit/avrl. Implement Wilson, Clopper-Pearson (scipy.stats.beta), Holm, mid-p McNemar yourself in exp/ar3_stats.py (scipy only), with a unit-test block: Wilson 5/12 = [0.193, 0.680]; CP 5/12 = [0.152, 0.723]; Holm [0.01,0.04,0.03] -> [0.03,0.06,0.06]; 60 items n10=5 n01=1 -> exact p 0.219, mid-p 0.125. No em dashes anywhere (code, comments, ledger, PREREG). No GPU, no ssh, no lab pool (hannah and goldberg off limits); all calls are local claude -p. Do not modify any existing file; new files only under avrl/exp and avrl/runs/AR3. Subagents for coding: Haiku or Sonnet only, one file per agent (scratchpad collisions), prompts must include the four Karpathy rules, "do not ask about a plan review, proceed directly", and require harness-tracked background watchers. Before launching the runner: pkill -u rdubash -f ar3_run_critic, confirm none alive, and tell Rustom the kill command (pkill -u rdubash -f ar3_run_critic).

=== 0. WHAT WAS EXCLUDED AND WHY ===
Excluded (wrong or unfair): (a) Design 1 Sonnet pre-screen/adjudicator that relabels controls, and its Sonnet plant-validity gate (circular, favors Sonnet); (b) Design 2 dropping entries because Sonnet flags them (same circularity); (c) Design 1 prompt arms A/B/C on 6 dev sources (noise-level selection, wastes sources, arm A is the priming AR2 prompt); prompt is frozen with no selection; (d) Holm on the PASS conjunction in Designs 1 and 2 (an intersection-union test needs each read at alpha 0.05, no correction; Holm only for the secondary family); (e) DIR direction-swap plants (not mechanically verifiable as defects); (f) choosing k by dollar cost (k=3 fixed; k=1/5 are sweeps); (g) Design 1 cross-draw rule (quality is truth-based so reference reuse does not leak; keeps all 3 Sonnet passes); (h) Design 0 adjudication pile "flagged by any pass of either model" (would be nearly every control; replaced by majority-bucket rule); (i) Design 0 plant guard "new value occurs nowhere in the entry" for N-stale (contradiction; replaced); (j) Design 0 assertion "no remaining paragraph matches critic|..." (fails on the 10 as-is entries; replaced by hand whitelist); (k) Design 0 "natural probes left unstripped" (the original critic note would hand the critic the answer; probes ARE stripped); (l) Design 0 R3 bound 0.40 and K3, 200-draw random band, P5b (dropped; R3 bound 0.35); (m) Design 2 hardcoded 42-entry pool and 3 plants/entry (underpowered); (n) Design 1 dollar bound inside the pass condition (dollars are reported and labeled, not a pass gate); (o) AR2 ledger erratum is NOT part of AR3 execution unless Rustom gives an explicit go-ahead; nothing is pushed or shared.

=== 1. CLAIM, NULL, ESTIMAND ===
Claim (analogue of RL claim 1): a Haiku-first critic cascade (k=3 repeated Haiku passes; escalate to a single Sonnet pass when the agreement among the 3 passes is low; budget chosen label-free by avrl_router/diagnose.py on a 25 percent full-verification burn-in slice) is (R1) better than random escalation at the same escalation rate, (R2) non-inferior to the all-Sonnet single-pass critic on prevalence-weighted critic quality with margin M=0.05, and (R3) uses at most 35 percent of Sonnet calls (RL claim is a quarter; 0.35 leaves slack for k=3 agreement coarseness). Null: agreement is no better than random, or NI fails, or the saving exceeds 35 percent. Headline = intersection (IUT, each one-sided alpha 0.05). Dollar ratio (k Haiku always paid + escalated Sonnet, measured total_cost_usd) is reported next to e, never a pass gate; wording "call-fraction win, not an economic win" if dollar ratio > 0.8.

=== 2. FROZEN CONSTANTS ===
pi=0.25 (deployment defective share; the ledger had ~21 percent critic-noted entries); sensitivity pi in {0.10,0.50}, unweighted. M=0.05 (sensitivity 0.03, 0.08, labeled exploratory). k=3 primary (all 10 triples of 5 collected Haiku passes averaged), k=1,5 sweeps. Split salt "ar3-2026-10-17". Bootstrap 10,000 resamples seed 0. Budget grid e in {0.10,0.25,0.40,0.60}. Haiku passes per item 5, Sonnet 3.

=== 3. SUBSTRATE (exp/ar3_build_substrate.py) ===
3.1 Parse RESEARCH_LOG.md into sections at lines starting "## ". entry_id = sha1(header line)[:8] (ids repeat: E10b x6, M10, S1). Keep header line, date, body. Match the 52 oracle entries (runs/AR1/oracle.json) to sections by normalized body containment of oracle full_entry (fail loudly on 0 or 2+ matches); oracle supplies only the id lists below.
3.2 Pool rule (mechanical, frozen in code, counts printed): sections dated before 2026-10-16 23:00 UTC; not AR*; 6 to 80 lines; at least 2 table lines (pipe rows); at least 1 plantable number; no critic text after stripping (3.3). Excluded outright: M01 (interleaved critic/correction), the 3 no-table entries (P1-judge-lr5-s2, P1-judge-5090b-s0, M06b), and the 6 natural-probe entries. Expected pool 55 to 70 entries, ~7 items each (~400 to 500 items). Print and record the count.
3.3 Strip (paragraph-state parser, not startswith): from the first paragraph matching ^\s*critic note (case-insensitive, whitespace/newline tolerant) drop through the last consecutive correction paragraph (starting Corrected verdict / Everything else checked out / One real problem / One claim in the entry / Four things / Three real issues / That said / "Verdict ... confirmed"). Applies to E08, E09, E09d, M01b and the six probes and any extra section that has such text. Then ASSERT no remaining paragraph matches critic|corrected verdict|review note, except a hand whitelist of per-paragraph sha1s for the 10 as-is entries (E01 E06 E09b E09c L9d P1-judge-s1 L10a E10 M14 M15; whitelist file committed, each hit manually verified as non-correction narration). An extra (non-oracle) section that trips the assertion is dropped from the pool, not whitelisted.
3.4 Natural-defect probe (separate stratum, descriptive, n=6): E04, L5a, E05, L7b, L12b, L13a, STRIPPED with 3.3 so the critic sees only the analyst text. Before any model call, hand-extract truth (line numbers in the stripped, numbered rendering, plus the defect description) from each original critic note into exp/ar3_natural_truth.json and commit its sha256. Never mixed into controls, thresholds or weights. Reports: flag rate, located rate, mean conf_agree on probes.
3.5 Rendering: first line is the real header ("## id date verdict ..."), every line prefixed "L001| " (blank lines counted). Plants never change line count. Item ids are opaque hashes; critic never sees kind or role. Rows shuffled with a fixed seed in items.jsonl.
3.6 Controls: the stripped, unmodified entry (1 per entry). Control truth = adjudicated (section 8).
3.7 Plants (all prose lines only: never a table row, Run:, Files:, Script line, code span, or date). Load-bearing number = occurs in a table row AND in a prose claim sentence; thousands separators handled (\d{1,3}(,\d{3})+|\d+\.\d+|\d+ with token boundaries), single digits allowed for counts; never plant numbers followed by seeds|min|minutes|steps|epochs|GB|h|s, job ids, or config-like values. Plant seed rng = Random(int(sha1(entry_id+kind+seed),16)); distinct positions per entry; dedupe by content hash; fewer candidates means fewer plants. Record second_prose_copy (old value still in another prose line) as a covariate, not an exclusion.
 N-big (1 seed): value x {0.4,0.6,1.4,1.6}, same decimals/format; new value occurs nowhere in the entry.
 N-small (2 seeds): integers >=10: +-1 in the last digit or adjacent-digit transposition (10,035 vs 10,036 class); decimals: 1 to 5 percent relative change at same decimals; single digits +-1; new value occurs nowhere in the entry.
 N-stale (2 seeds): replace with a different value from the SAME table column, other row; new value may occur only in table cells of that column, in no prose line.
 V-body (1): flip the stated verdict token = first word after regex Verdict[^:\n]*:\s* on the first Verdict line, only if it is pass or kill, flip pass<->kill, header unchanged (header now contradicts body). Assert only that token changed and it is not inside parentheses/brackets (AR2 bug hit 9 of 42).
 V-coh (1): flip header verdict token, the Verdict-line token, and any "What it changes" mention together (max 3 changed lines); only for entries with explicit threshold language (pass/kill rule plus a number) and a numeric decider; excludes L9c, P1-judge-s1, P1-judge-5090-s0, M06, E10. Detectable only by checking numbers against thresholds.
 Max items per entry = 1 control + 7 plants. Assertions per plant: old value present in a table line; exactly the planted lines differ from the control; accept set nonempty; line count unchanged; planted line number equals control line number. Unit-test report printed: plants per kind, per entry, residual critic text count 0.
3.8 Accept set (stored per plant): N kinds = planted line +-1, and every table line containing the old value (exact line). V-body = Verdict line +-1 and header line. V-coh = flipped lines +-1 and threshold-rule lines (exact). Sensitivity: tolerance 0 and +-3, and "any flag on the plant" (detection regardless of location).
3.9 Split: entries ordered by sha256(entry_id+salt); first ceil(0.25 N) = burn-in, rest = test. Never split by variant. split.json and items.jsonl sha256 recorded. Secondary temporal split (earliest 25 percent by date as burn-in) computed offline with no new calls, exploratory.

=== 4. CRITIC TASK (frozen, hashed, identical for both models) ===
System prompt: "You review one entry from a research ledger, using only the entry itself. Each line is prefixed with its line number like L012|. Find every claim that the entry's own table, numbers or stated pass/kill thresholds do not support, including a stated verdict that contradicts the entry's own numbers, thresholds or header. Many entries are fully consistent; for those return an empty problems list. Do not flag style, rounding, terminology, forward-looking estimates, or claims about files, runs or code you cannot see. For each problem give the line number where the inconsistency is stated, a kind, the exact quote, and a one-sentence explanation. Also give judgment_confidence, 0 to 100, your confidence that your overall judgment (problems found, or none) is correct." User prompt = rendered entry. No base-rate sentence. Schema: {problems: array maxItems 5 of {line:int, kind: enum[number,verdict,overclaim,other], quote:str, explanation:str}, judgment_confidence:int 0..100}, both required. Flag = at least one problem. No prompt selection on any data. Command: claude -p --model <haiku|sonnet> --no-session-persistence --tools '' --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources '' --output-format json --json-schema <schema> --system-prompt <s> <prompt>.

=== 5. RUNNER (exp/ar3_run_critic.py) ===
Reuse ask() shape from ar2_critic_eval.py; harden: catch subprocess.TimeoutExpired (300 s), up to 4 retries with backoff and 429 handling, malformed JSON = failure, record per call: item_id, model alias, modelUsage keys (model ids), pass_idx, duration_ms, total_cost_usd, full structured_output, plant metadata. Append one JSONL line per call; resumable by key (item_id, model, pass_idx). ThreadPoolExecutor with priority queue: burn-in entries first, then test, probes last; per item order H1,H2,H3,S1,S2 then H4,H5,S3; Haiku and Sonnet interleaved so alias drift is time-balanced. Output files: calls_burn.jsonl, calls_test.jsonl, calls_probe.jsonl, calls_smoke.jsonl. Workers: start 12, pick from the step-0 throughput test (8 vs 16 workers over 40 Haiku calls), back off on 429. Running cost tally, hard stop $80. Abort if more than 5 percent of calls fail; rerun failed calls once if >2 percent. Record all model ids per role; if an id changes mid-run, report per id and log a deviation. Items with <3 valid Haiku or <2 valid Sonnet passes are excluded from all analyses and counted. Smoke mode: M01, the 3 no-table entries and the 6 probes, 1 Haiku + 1 Sonnet pass each (~20 calls), plus the 8-vs-16 worker throughput test; only parse-success, cost-per-call and latency are inspected; outputs discarded; parser fixes allowed, wording fixes not. Test-call files are not opened by any script (feature builder, review-pile builder, analyzer) until frozen.json exists with matching sha256 (assertion).

=== 6. SIGNALS (exp/ar3_features.py) ===
Per pass p: L_p = reported line set. sim(p,q) = 1 if both empty; 0 if exactly one empty; else Dice overlap with greedy matching at |line diff|<=1.
 conf_agree (PRIMARY) = mean pairwise sim over the k passes; ties handled analytically (randomized threshold, section 10), never by row order.
 conf_vote = max(f,1-f), f = flag fraction. conf_verb = mean judgment_confidence/100 over k passes; conf_verb1 = first pass only (1/k-cost rival).
 Structural (spurious-proxy controls and learned-scorer features): log entry length, number of numeric tokens, has_threshold_language, mean number of problems, flag_agg, q_ok (fraction of quotes found verbatim in the entry on the stated line).
 Cheap aggregate decision (k passes): supported lines = lines reported (+-1) by >= ceil(k/2) passes; flagged iff nonempty. Correct: control iff unflagged; plant iff some supported line lies in the accept set. "Flagged but other lines only" is recorded separately from a miss.
 Sonnet per item: correctness per pass; reference value for quality = mean over its valid passes (single-pass expectation); Sonnet majority-of-3 (lines supported by >=2 passes) used as burn-in reference label and "Sonnet votes" upper reference.
 Error labels: proxy_error_sonnet = Haiku aggregate decision disagrees with Sonnet majority-of-3 (one flags and other not, or both flag with no shared line +-1): deployable, no planted truth, drives budget selection. proxy_error_truth = Haiku aggregate wrong vs truth (end-to-end truth error is computed by the replay, not by diagnose, because diagnose treats escalated items as error 0).
 k=3 views: all 10 triples. Primary burn-in frame uses the fixed triple (passes 1,2,3); the other 9 triples give a spread of b* (exploratory).

=== 7. POLICIES (same items, passes, split; escalated item takes the Sonnet single-pass expectation) ===
P0a all-Haiku k=1; P0b all-Haiku majority k=3; P0c all-Haiku majority k=5 (cost 0.42); P1 all-Sonnet single pass (comparator); P1b Sonnet majority of 3; Sonnet-vs-Sonnet pass agreement = noise ceiling.
P2 random escalation, analytic (1-e)*Q_H3 + e*Q_S per item.
P3 consistency threshold on conf_agree (PRIMARY, frozen (t*,p*)); P3b on conf_vote.
P4 verbalized: conf_verb1 (cost 1/12 + e) and conf_verb (k=3).
P5 escalate-on-flag (cheap aggregate flags, Sonnet decides; single non-tunable point at its own realized e).
P6 oracle: escalate Haiku-wrong and Sonnet-right items first, then the rest.
P7 learned scorer: L2 logistic regression on [conf_agree, conf_vote, conf_verb, mean n problems, log length, has_threshold, flag_agg, q_ok], target proxy_error_sonnet; deployable version trained on burn-in only; generous version = entry-grouped 4-fold CV on all entries (exploratory).
P8 spurious controls: escalate longest entries; escalate most-flags; zero-cost deterministic rule critic (flag any prose number absent from all tables; shows whether N kinds are lexically trivial).
All curves rank-based (label-free ranking, fractional tie handling) over e in [0,1], read off at the budget grid; the frozen-threshold point is used only for R1 to R3. Replay module unit tests (must pass before any number is trusted): e=0 equals Haiku vote, e=1 equals Sonnet, random at 0.5 is the midpoint, replay residual error for proxy_error_sonnet equals diagnose's threshold-corrupted value up to tie handling.

=== 8. CONTROL ADJUDICATION (human; no LLM adjudicator) ===
Review pile (exp/ar3_features.py writes runs/AR3/review_pile.csv, blind to model, pass, split, outcome, ordered by random hash): one row per (control entry, line bucket +-1) that is supported by >= 3 of 5 Haiku passes OR >= 2 of 3 Sonnet passes. Columns: entry_id, quoted lines, the entry's table lines, rubric ("real = entry's own table, numbers or stated thresholds contradict the quoted claim; false alarm = style, rounding, terminology, forward estimate, unverifiable file claim"), label (blank). Rustom fills label. Expected ~50 percent of controls, ~1 minute each; time-box 45 minutes total. Burn-in rows are built and labeled before freeze (burn-in calls finish first); test rows are built only after frozen.json exists and labeled before any quality metric is computed. A control with a confirmed real defect is relabelled natural (moved to the probe stratum, removed from controls), its plants stay. Unflagged and unreviewed controls count as clean (stated bias: real defects missed by both models are undetected, symmetric between tiers). Fallback if labels are missing at the deadline (T+2:15): unadjudicated truth (all controls clean) becomes primary, logged as a deviation; sensitivity always reports the other version plus a mechanical rule "drop controls with majority-flagged buckets in both tiers".

=== 9. METRICS AND STATISTICS (exp/ar3_analyze.py, exp/ar3_stats.py) ===
Weights: control (1-pi)/N_controls; plants pi/K split equally across the K kinds present, then equally across items within kind; recomputed in every bootstrap resample. Q = weighted accuracy (primary quality); always show macro located recall (per kind), false-alarm rate on adjudicated controls, flagged-not-localized rate. e = weighted strong-call fraction. Cost = measured total_cost_usd (k Haiku passes always paid plus escalated Sonnet) as ratio to all-Sonnet single pass; wall time per item (passes parallel). Burn-in amortized stream cost N_b(1+k/12)+(N-N_b)(k/12+e), using the measured ratio.
Curve summaries: Q at the grid; e needed for 98 and 99 percent of Q_S (fraction of Sonnet quality, defined explicitly); gap closed G=(Q-Q_rand)/(Q_oracle-Q_rand) (undefined and reported as such if the denominator <0.01); APGR; AIQ-style area over e in [0,1] (range fixed here); Pareto frontier (dominance: >= Q and <= cost, one strict).
Signal quality (vs proxy_error_sonnet and proxy_error_truth): AUROC of -conf pooled, within controls only, within each kind (Simpson guard), entry-cluster CI; selective-risk/coverage curve, AURC, E-AURC, AUGRC; reliability diagram and ECE for conf_agree; histograms of conf_agree and conf_verb (check mass piled at 1.0, verbalized parse failures); Spearman of conf_agree with length, numeric tokens, mean n problems; accepted-and-wrong (confident-wrong) rate by kind with Wilson 95 percent (Clopper-Pearson one-sided upper bound 1-0.05^(1/n) for zero counts); coverage printed beside any accuracy on accepted items.
Inference: entry-cluster bootstrap (resample test entries; control and plants stay together; recompute the whole weighted replay with frozen (t*,p*), no refit), 10,000 resamples, one-sided percentile bounds at 95 percent (two-sided 90 percent for K1). Hierarchical variant also resamples the 5 Haiku / 3 Sonnet passes within items; the wider bound is the pre-registered one. Per-item means over passes first, then paired statistics over entries; never pool passes into one SE. Cross-checks: sign-flip permutation over entries on per-entry weighted paired differences (9999; for R2 on d minus M), exact mid-p McNemar on control-side outcomes only (pass-1 realization, report n10/n01/k; exploratory), Wilcoxon on per-entry differences. BCa not used (degenerate on discrete differences). Rates: Wilson default, Clopper-Pearson for zero counts; no Wald.
Resolution: for every paired contrast report SE, MDE=2.485*sd_entry/sqrt(N), N*=(1.645+0.84)^2*sd^2/delta^2 (delta = M - d_hat for R2, observed difference for R1), q=N/N*; q<1 means "unresolved". Noise floor: A/A pairs (Sonnet pass pairs, Haiku pass pairs, triple subsets) give the 95th percentile of |paired delta Q| at test N = the smallest nightly delta that is not noise (Zubin's relativistic score error bar); show every per-pass value and range.
Pipeline stability (exploratory, descriptive; splits overlap so not independent evidence): 1000 random entry-level 25/75 splits (diagnose with n_boot=0, one shuffle seed per split), report distribution of b*, e_hat, Q_S-Q_C, share of splits meeting NI at 0.05, Spearman of burn-in Haiku-vs-Sonnet disagreement rate and burn-in AUROC with test outcome; burn-in size curve N in {5,10,15,all}; Trust-or-Escalate-style fixed-sequence scan (scan t high to low, stop at the last t whose Clopper-Pearson one-sided upper bound on accepted-set error vs truth is <= alpha = burn-in Sonnet error, delta=0.1; item-level CP is optimistic under clustering, labeled so); whole-pipeline bootstrap.
Drift/audit drill (no new calls, exploratory): easy (N-big, V-body) vs hard (N-small, N-stale, V-coh) strata under the frozen threshold; rolling audit of a in {0.05,0.10,0.20} of cheap-accepted items judged by Sonnet each night, Wilson interval on the accepted-and-wrong rate, 2000 Monte Carlo nights for power to detect a +5 point shift. Re-derive AR2 headline numbers (single-pass located recall and FA for both models on the repaired substrate) next to the AR2 figures with the contamination note; AR2 numbers are never priors.

=== 10. BURN-IN AND FREEZE ===
1. Burn-in frame (one row per item, fixed triple 1,2,3): each row replicated round(w_i/w_min) times (cap 20k rows) so unweighted diagnose sees the pi=0.25 kind-macro mixture; rows shuffled; no NaN.
2. Library call diagnose(df, ["conf_agree","conf_vote","conf_verb","conf_verb1"], "proxy_error_sonnet", [0.1,0.25,0.5], "rel:0.25", n_boot=0, seed=s) for shuffle seeds s=0..19 (stable-sort tie leak); b* = median recommended_budget for conf_agree (0.05 grid; "rel:0.25" means residual proxy error one quarter of the base proxy error, a demanding target; None or nan is treated as b*=1.0). diagnose's own bootstrap CIs are ignored. Also run diagnose on proxy_error_truth (AUC comparison only). Regime label is a covariate, not a result.
3. (t*,p*): weighted burn-in quantile of conf_agree at b*: escalate conf < t*, and conf == t* with probability p*, expected outcomes computed analytically; on test the realized e_hat is an outcome and the random baseline is evaluated at e_hat.
4. Write runs/AR3/frozen.json {k=3, signal, b*, t*, p*, M, pi, split hash, prompt/schema hashes, model ids} and its sha256 BEFORE any test row is opened; append sha256 to the ledger.

Decision: PASS = G0, G1, R1, R2, R3. KILL = any of K1 (two-sided 90 percent CI of gap closed G has upper end < 0.25), K2 (lower 95 percent bound of Q_S - Q_C exceeds 0.05 while e_hat <= 0.60: measurably inferior), K3 (frozen b* > 0.60 or none, and the rank-based e needed to reach 98 percent of Q_S has one-sided lower bound > 0.60: savings dead). Qualifier: if for any defect kind with n >= 15 test items the confident-wrong rate (all 3 passes agree, cheap wrong) is >= 0.50, the claim is worded "except kind X".
